text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 severity varies widely, from asymptomatic cases to severe illness, including pneumonia, organ failure, and even death. Symptoms can range from mild (fever, cough, fatigue) to severe, and can appear 2-14 days after exposure. Anyone experiencing difficulty breathing should seek immediate medical attention, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). While most people recover without long-term effects, some experience lingering issues.

list.snippet: Mild Cases: Symptoms like fever, cough, fatigue, and sore throat are common.
Moderate Cases: May include difficulty breathing and mild pneumonia.
Severe Cases: Characterized by severe pneumonia, organ failure, and potential death.
Asymptomatic Cases: Individuals may be infected without showing any symptoms.
Progression: Symptoms can start mild and progress to more severe stages.
Individual Variation: The severity of COVID-19 can differ significantly from person to person.
Risk Factors: Certain populations, such as the elderly and those with underlying health conditions, may be at higher risk of severe illness.
Seeking Help: Difficulty breathing warrants immediate medical attention.
Prevention: Measures like good indoor ventilation, physical distancing, and masking can help reduce transmission.
